transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well, I suppose what finally pushed me to come in is this constant tightness I’ve been having. My neck and shoulders, and even my jaw, feel clenched almost all the time. It’s like I’m bracing for bad news, even when nothing’s happening—just sitting at my desk marking papers, or trying to watch TV in the evening. 

I kept thinking it would pass, you know, like maybe I’d slept funny or spent too long leaning over lesson plans, but it just seems to be there most of the time now.
Have you experienced any particularly stressful or traumatic events recently that might be contributing to how you're feeling?

Well, traumatic feels like a big word, but there was that pipe bursting at home about seven months ago. It flooded part of the place, and then the remodeling just turned the house upside down. Contractors in and out, dust everywhere, things moved into boxes—I couldn’t find half my shirts for weeks, which sounds silly, but it wore me down.

So… yes, I think that’s when this all really started, around then. The house has been in chaos since, and I don’t think I’ve settled back down properly.
Have you noticed that your anxiety or worry extends beyond the situation with the house, such as concerns about work, health, or other responsibilities, even when there isn't an immediate problem?

Yes, it does. It’s not just the house anymore, though that’s where my mind tends to start. I’ll be thinking, did the contractors miss something, is there going to be another problem hiding behind a wall or under the floorboards… and then suddenly I’m thinking about school.

Like, whether my lesson plans are slipping, whether the robotics club kids are falling behind because I haven’t been as organized as I usually am. And then it turns into, am I letting my wife down, am I letting the family down because I’m not keeping everything under control. It’s like my mind just hops from one thing to the next before I’ve even finished worrying about the first one.
Do you find it hard to control or stop your worrying, even when you try to focus on something else?

Yes… yes, I do. I’ll tell myself, right, focus on the class in front of you, you’re explaining something, pay attention to the students. And then one little thing pops up—like remembering an invoice that’s late, or noticing a student hasn’t turned something in—and suddenly I’m off.

Not out loud, usually, but in my head it becomes this whole chain of what-ifs. What if the invoice means there’s another problem, what if I’ve missed something important, what if that student is falling behind and I should’ve caught it sooner… and then I’m barely listening to my own thoughts properly, if that makes sense.

I try to shut it down, but it doesn’t really switch off just because I tell it to.
Have you noticed any other physical symptoms, like stomach problems, headaches, or trouble sleeping, that seem to be related to this constant worry?

Yes—well, the main thing is this tightness. My neck and shoulders are just… locked up most of the time now. And my jaw too, which I didn’t really notice at first until I caught myself sitting at my desk with my teeth clenched.

I suppose that’s actually what finally made me come in. It feels like I’m bracing for bad news even when nothing is happening—just sitting there marking papers, or even trying to watch TV at night. I’ll realize I’m hunched up like I’m waiting for something to go wrong.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried most days, even when nothing specific is happening to cause it?

Yes… most days, I’d say. Even if nothing is actually happening right then, my head finds something to latch onto.

It’ll start with the house—whether the contractors missed something, or there’s some problem we haven’t spotted—and then before I know it I’m thinking about school, whether my lesson plans are slipping, or whether the robotics club kids are behind. Then it sort of widens out into, am I disappointing my wife, am I letting the family down because I’m not keeping everything under control.

It’s like there doesn’t have to be a real crisis in front of me. My mind just keeps moving around looking for one.
Have you been having trouble sleeping or feeling unusually tired lately, even if you’re not doing anything physically demanding?

Yes, tired, definitely. I mean, teaching is tiring anyway—people think you just stand at the front and talk, but there’s the planning, the marking, chasing things up, the little dramas in corridors… sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

It’s more than normal tired. By the time the last bell goes, I feel completely wrung out. And then I’ll bring home what should be a small stack of quizzes, nothing dramatic, and it feels like I’m pushing through mud just to get through them.

Even if I’ve had what should count as a decent night, or a quiet Sunday, I don’t feel properly restored. It’s like the tiredness is already waiting for me.
Do you often feel restless or like you’re constantly on edge, as if you can’t quite relax even when you want to?

Yes… yes, that’s a good way to put it. I feel wound up most of the day, like I’m sort of waiting for the next thing to go wrong.

At school I’ll catch myself pacing around the classroom between lessons, even when there’s nothing I actually need to be doing. Or I’ll check my phone between periods to see if there’s a message from the contractor, and then if there isn’t one I’m still thinking, well, does that mean something’s gone quiet because there’s a problem?

It’s not like I’m choosing to be on alert. I’ll sit down meaning to relax for a minute, and then I’m up again, moving around or checking something. It’s exhausting, honestly.
Do you feel like your worrying has become a constant habit, something that just seems to run in the background even when you're not actively thinking about the house or work?

Yes, it does feel like it’s just… always running somewhere in the back.

Even if I’m not deliberately sitting there thinking, “Right, now I’ll worry about the house,” my mind sort of jumps there anyway—like, did the contractors miss something, is there some problem hidden behind a wall or under the floorboards. And then it’ll hop to school, whether my lesson plans are getting a bit thin, whether the robotics club kids are falling behind.

And then—this sounds a bit dramatic, maybe—but it turns into this bigger thing about whether I’m disappointing my wife, or the family, because I’m not keeping everything properly under control. It’s like one of those browser tabs you forget is open, except it’s using up all the energy in the background.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment out of things you used to like, like hobbies, time with family, or even teaching the robotics club?

I’m not sure, actually. I mean, I still do things, if that makes sense. I still turn up, still go through the motions.

The robotics club… I don’t know, some weeks the kids are excited about a little motor finally working and I do feel something, because they’re proud of themselves. But then I’m also thinking about whether we’ve got enough parts, or whether I remembered to book the room, or—sorry, that’s probably not what you asked.

With family, I’m there, but I don’t know if I’m enjoying it less or if I’m just distracted. My wife will put something on, or we’ll have dinner, and I’ll realize I’ve missed half the conversation because my mind’s wandered off. So… I wouldn’t say I don’t enjoy anything anymore. I just don’t always feel properly present for it.
Have you found yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually care about, even for short periods during the day?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say “hopeless,” exactly. That feels like quite a big word.

I do get low in patches, I suppose, but then I start thinking, well, anyone would if they’d been dealing with builders and school stuff and all the little things that pile up. Our kitchen still has this one cupboard door that doesn’t quite close properly, and every time I see it I think, should I have caught that earlier, should I ring someone, and then I’ve lost track of what I was doing.

So… sorry, I’m wandering. I haven’t really noticed a clear loss of interest, no. It’s more that I’m preoccupied, if that makes sense, rather than not caring.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on very quickly, like your heart racing, feeling short of breath, or thinking something terrible is about to happen?

I’m not sure I’d call it “sudden,” exactly. I mean, I do get worked up, but it’s usually because my mind has been chewing on something for a while, if that makes sense.

Like if I’m thinking about the house stuff, or something at school, it can build and build, and then I realize I’m tense and on edge. But I don’t think I’ve had those… out of nowhere attacks where it’s suddenly this huge wave of fear. At least, not that I’ve noticed.

Sometimes I wonder if I’d even recognize it properly, because I tend to explain it away as, “Well, of course I’m stressed, there’s a lot going on.” But no, I can’t think of a clear episode like that.
Would you say that you experience excessive anxiety and worry more days than not, even beyond the specific stressors like the house or work issues?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I keep telling myself it’s just because there’s a lot going on, but it doesn’t really stay in one box.

My mind jumps from the contractors and whether they’ve missed something in the house, to whether my lesson plans are slipping, to whether the robotics kids are falling behind because I haven’t planned properly. And then I’ll be thinking, am I letting my wife down, or the family, because I’m not keeping everything under control.

It’s not always one big thing, it’s more like… as soon as one worry quiets down, another one sort of takes its place.
Do you often notice that your muscle tension or physical symptoms, like tightness in your neck and shoulders, happen even when there’s no clear reason or stressor present?

Yes, that’s actually one of the main reasons I finally booked this appointment.

My neck and shoulders are tight almost all the time now, and my jaw too. It’s like I’m bracing myself, if that makes sense, like waiting for someone to tell me something’s gone wrong. And it happens even when I’m just sitting at my desk, not even doing anything particularly stressful, or when I’m trying to watch television in the evening.

I’ll catch myself sort of clenching, and then I think, why am I doing that? Nothing’s happening right now. But my body doesn’t seem to have got the message.
